messages:
support_jane: hi folks — customer reporting repeated 502s + high p95 on POST /v1/generate. Customer gave request_id `r-7b3c9a` and trace `trace-1f4`. Incident timestamp: 2026-03-15T16:22:04Z. Can eng/sre help with server-side log lookup + quick repro guidance? They can run curl if we give steps.

eng_oncall_mike: thanks, Jane. Can you confirm the full request_id string (any prefix/suffix)? also which region/stack (prod/dedicated)?

support_jane: full request_id from customer is `r-7b3c9a` (they copied from x-request-id header). Region: prod eu-west-1 (hosted). Customer says it happens ~1 in 20 calls, usually with payloads ~1.2k tokens.

sre_ash: jumping in. Quick search queries to run:
- Datadog logs: `service:gateway AND request_id:r-7b3c9a`
- Kibana/ES: `request_id:\"r-7b3c9a\" OR headers.x-request-id:\"r-7b3c9a\"`
- Splunk: `index=prod_logs request_id=\"r-7b3c9a\"`
If you have host access, on-box grep: `grep -R \"r-7b3c9a\" /var/log/redwood/* | tail -n 200`
Note retention: hot logs are kept 30d, cold archive 180d (search across cold requires async restore). If the request is >30d old, we need to pull an archived segment — will take ~30m.

eng_oncall_mike: also look for trace id: `trace-1f4` in APM. Example dd query for traces: `service:api AND trace_id:trace-1f4`

support_jane: customer can reproduce. They asked for a curl snippet to hit the same path — sending below (auth masked):
```bash
curl -i \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate\" \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>\" \
  -H \"X-Request-ID: r-7b3c9a\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-large","input":"<~1.2k token payload>","max_tokens":512}'
```

customer_lloyd: happy to run that — replacing token with my key now. I'll paste the exact curl I ran once done.

sre_ash: I pulled a quick hit in logs — seeing an upstream 502 from the model-serving pool around the same timestamp. snippet: 
```
2026-03-15T16:22:04.123Z INFO proxy request_id=r-7b3c9a route=/v1/generate status=502 upstream=pod-23-abc error=UpstreamTimeout
2026-03-15T16:22:04.124Z DEBUG request_id=r-7b3c9a backend=kv-cache hit=false latency_ms=1201
2026-03-15T16:22:04.125Z ERROR request_id=r-7b3c9a model-alloc=timeout details=alloc_wait_exceeded
```
If that's right, it looks like a short model-side allocation stall. Next steps: get full trace (APM) and model-worker logs for `pod-23-abc`.

eng_oncall_mike: yep — if you can get the full worker logs we can confirm OOM vs allocation queue. Commands if you have kube access: `kubectl logs pod-23-abc -n inference --since=10m` or `kubectl logs -p pod-23-abc` for previous container.

support_jane: i don't have kube access for prod. What do you need from me to fetch logs via SRE runbook?

sre_ash: open a temporary support debug bundle request to the customer (it contains request/headers/APM links + sanitized env info). Steps for the customer to run if we need client-side reproducible trace:
1) run their curl with `X-Request-ID: r-7b3c9a` (they already will)
2) if possible, capture response headers and full response body
3) run our debug helper (they can paste the following):
```bash
# generates a small bundle we can ingest (scrubs tokens)
curl -s https://api.redwood.example/debug/bundle \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: r-7b3c9a' \
  -o debug-r-7b3c9a.tar.gz
```
We will request the team to ingest that bundle — it helps correlate client timing with server spans.

devex_tam: FYI the debug bundle pipeline strips Authorization header values but preserves header keys and sizes. It also redacts full-text user inputs if user requests scrubbing — so tell the customer to mark anything sensitive.

billing_robin: unrelated but note: if the request retried multiple times, customer might see duplicate charges — check for `billing_event:attempt` in the logs for r-7b3c9a.

deploy_bot: deployment notice: inference-pool v2.3.1 rolled out eu-west-1 on 2026-03-14 02:00UTC. No known regressions but tagging in case.

support_jane: Lloyd pasted the exact curl and response headers:
```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2026 16:22:04 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-ID: r-7b3c9a
X-Trace-ID: trace-1f4

{"error":"UpstreamTimeout","message":"model worker allocation timed out"}
```

sre_ash: perfect. I've attached the worker logs request to eng-runtime and asked for lookups on `pod-23-abc`. If they confirm it's allocation pressure we'll propose: pin to a higher-memory pool or retry with a slightly higher timeout.

eng_oncall_mike: action items:
- support_jane: ask Lloyd to upload debug bundle if he can (command above).
- sre_ash: follow up on worker logs + APM spans, check ephemeral disk/alloc queue metrics around 16:22.
- eng_runtime: please prioritize `pod-23-abc` logs for 16:15-16:30 UTC and share any OOM/alloc traces.

customer_lloyd: debug bundle uploaded to the link you gave (file `debug-r-7b3c9a.tar.gz`). Let me know if you need anything else.

audit_bot: bundle `debug-r-7b3c9a.tar.gz` received and queued for ingestion (id: dbg-5544). Access limited to SRE + Eng-Oncall.

sre_ash: ingestion done — found model-worker stack trace matching alloc_wait_exceeded. Not OOM, looks like allocation queue length spiked when pool autoscaler was slightly behind. See metrics snippet: `alloc_queue_len=47 at t=2026-03-15T16:21:58Z` (normal <5).

eng_oncall_mike: linking this to autoscale lag. For short-term mitigation, recommend a fallback policy: on alloc_wait_exceeded return an informative 429 or retry with backoff for user. For this customer we've applied a temporary routing to a warmer pool.

support_jane: sent Lloyd the update and the mitigation note. He asked if logs older than 30d would be searchable — he had an older incident from Feb.

sre_ash: reminder: hot logs 30d. Feb incident would be >30d so it's in cold archive — we can restore but it'll take ~20-40m and has limited search coverage. If the customer needs that historic trace, ask for the old request_id and we can kick an archive restore.

support_jane: thanks everyone — tagging for follow-up if anything else shows up. :thumbsup:

eng_oncall_mike: noted. I'll close once eng-runtime confirms no infra regression. :eyes:
